summary: The retro's authoritative milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 experiment commits since activation, so the locked numeric fields stay 0 (conductor-owned). But on-disk ground truth read this turn contradicts that 0: results/experiment_4432..4441_*.json (10 artifacts, mtimes 2026-06-19T06:29:16->09:14:59 EDT, ~2h46m wall window) plus the ops/changelog window show milestone 2026.06.410 fully ran, with a clean/unflagged capstone (exp4441, paper_ready=true). The 0 is therefore the recurring false-zero milestone-scoped-timing-detector gap (documented .363-.407, now extending to .410) -- an observability artifact, NOT a genuinely empty milestone or a stalled launch.
bottlenecks_identified: RECURRING (6+ consecutive milestones, .363-.407, now .410): the milestone-scoped timing detector false-zeroed -- it attributed 0 commits since activation while 10 experiment artifacts (exp4432-exp4441) sit on disk with mtimes spanning ~2h46m and a clean capstone. The bottleneck is observability, not execution.

GPU idle (both RTX 3090s at 0% util, 4MB allocated) is NOT flagged as a bottleneck: the detector attributed 0 compute-bound tasks, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null per the GPU-idle interpretation rule (idle GPUs are correct when no compute-bound task is attributed). NOTE this idle reading is itself downstream of the same false-zero -- it cannot be trusted to mean the run used no GPU.

Because the detector returns 0, every operational retro for these milestones is forced to reconstruct ground truth by hand from on-disk mtimes + the changelog window, which is slow and erodes trust in the retro's own numeric fields.
improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector: replace the commit-attribution scan with an mtime scan of results/experiment_*.json since milestone activation, plus an ops/changelog-window fallback, so experiments that landed (but were not attributed by commit) are counted.

Add write-time stamping of duration_s and a compute_bound flag onto every experiment artifact (in the experiment template / conductor), so the retro can populate slowest_experiments and total_wall_time_minutes directly from artifacts rather than re-deriving from filesystem mtimes.

Emit detector_gap_suspected=true automatically whenever the timing detector reports 0 BUT results/experiment_*.json artifacts exist on disk in the milestone window -- so a false-zero is self-flagged instead of being silently reported as an empty milestone.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the false-zero milestone-scoped timing detector (mtime scan + changelog-window fallback + detector_gap_suspected emission). This single fix removes the recurring observability failure that has degraded every operational retro from .363 through .410.

Stamp duration_s + compute_bound at artifact write-time so slowest_experiments and total_wall_time_minutes become directly computable, restoring the retro's ability to surface real wall-time bottlenecks.

Until the detector is fixed, keep cross-checking on-disk artifacts (results/experiment_*.json mtimes + changelog) before concluding a milestone is empty -- a 0 from the detector must be treated as suspect, not authoritative.
meta_reflection: No experiment wall-time was wasted this milestone -- the 10 .410 experiments ran cleanly (exp4432-exp4441, capstone unflagged, paper_ready=true). The waste is purely analytic and recurring: the timing detector has false-zeroed for 6+ consecutive milestones, so each retro must reconstruct ground truth by hand. The lesson is process-level -- the operational failure here is observability, not execution -- and the standing highest-leverage fix is repairing the detector (mtime scan + changelog fallback + self-flagged detector_gap_suspected). estimated_time_savings_pct is 0 because the fix saves analytic/operator time and trust, not experiment compute.
